text: Reading Passage 1 has six sections, A-F.
Choose the correct heading for each section from the list of headings below.

list: Research findings concerning achievements in maths
The typical format of a maths lesson
Background to middle-years education in Japan
The key to Japanese successes in maths education

items: There is a wider range of achievement amongst English pupils studying maths than amongst their Japanese counterparts.
The percentage of Gross National Product spent on education generally reflects the level of attainment in mathematics.
Private schools in Japan are more modern and spacious than state-run lower secondary schools.
Teachers mark homework in Japanese schools.

items.title: Maths textbooks in Japanese schools are
options: well organised and adapted to the needs of the pupils.
written to be used in conjunction with TV programmes.
not very popular with many Japanese teachers.

items.title: When a new maths topic is introduced,
options: students answer questions on the board.
students rely entirely on the textbook.
it is carefully and patiently explained to the students.
it is usual for students to use extra worksheets.

items.title: How do schools deal with students who experience difficulties?
options: They are given appropriate supplementary tuition.
They are encouraged to copy from other pupils.
They are forced to explain their slow progress.
They are placed in a mixed-ability class.

items.title: Why do Japanese students tend to achieve relatively high rates of success in maths?
options: It is a compulsory subject in Japan.
They are used to working without help from others.
Much effort is made and correct answers are emphasised.
There is a strong emphasis on repetitive learning.
